analysis: The broad option provides Python, data preparation, statistical learning and algorithm design alongside survey, qualitative and experimental research. Mathematics supports model development. Econometrics and evidence synthesis strengthen evaluation. Social psychology, governance and policy analysis establish the social and policy problems these tools address. Entrepreneurship and digital transformation give design and implementation perspectives, while applied sustainability research and persuasive communication give partner-facing experience. The active workbook does not support a dedicated web-development or agent-based modelling sequence. Organisational strategy and persuasion offer complementary contributions rather than substitutes for UvA digital prototypes.

The climate option combines climate processes and risk, geospatial data and planning, and social investigation of environmental decisions. Earth Observation builds data collection and GIS methods. Spatial Planning applies them to concrete environmental problems. Climate Change, hazards, delta and energy design provide domains for their use, and qualitative research, comparative politics, sustainability governance and policy analysis support study of stakeholders and public decisions. Dynamic Earth, soils and resource geology were removed because they offered less relevant coverage for the concept. A mobility systems project is specific to UvA and is not inferred from GIS or spatial planning.

The responsible AI option integrates programming and data management, regression and classification, neural networks, and ethics. Law and rights, research design, critical sociology, media and environmental justice provide ways to examine who is affected by data and technology. Environmental justice supplies a concrete domain for studying unequal impacts and collective response. AI Ethics explicitly covers bias, surveillance and responsibility. Media & Race contributes research on representation and power. The technical courses teach modelling and its evaluation; they do not independently supply ethics or establish responsible implementation.

All three plans address the same external target and have different advanced priorities. The broad option centres social evidence and intervention design, the climate option centres spatial evidence and environmental decisions, and the AI option centres technical models and questions of power. Health technology remains an evidenced alternative direction, with less direct coverage in these options; the completed set reaches the maximum.
constructionStop: Three academically viable and distinct compositions meet the maximum.

BENECON312.contribution: Uses regression, instrumental variables and simulation to distinguish causal questions from prediction in an empirical paper.
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

alignment.rationale: Both teach data preparation and visualisation. UCR uses R in a dedicated data science course, while UvA combines these skills with Python and social research projects.
Both build and evaluate predictive models. UvA combines modelling with stakeholder engagement and analysis of algorithmic bias.
Both analyse stakeholders and develop policy responses to complex systems. UCR focuses on sustainability governance. UvA develops an intervention plan for a health or mobility system.
Both involve team research on a problem from an external partner. UCR investigates a regional sustainability question. UvA also implements a digital intervention in its final semester.
Both use design thinking and prototyping. UCR tests a venture idea, while UvA tests a digital intervention for behaviour change.
The fifth semester offers 30 EC of elective study, a minor, an approved internship or study abroad.
